answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by giving every new identity a small transaction quota that grows only through a long history of successful, attested trades. A lantern of public reputation lights each account's record, so a fresh fake starts dim and capped, while a haven of trusted counterparties forms slowly around honest agents. Splitting effort across many identities keeps each one weak, since quota cannot be bought or transferred, and the only inlet to higher limits is months of real, verifiable work.
